chunks: 3933 - It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, who said:

A man wrote to al-Faqīh عليه السلام concerning a man who gave a garment to the fuller to process it, then the fuller gave it to another fuller to process it, and the garment was lost. Is it obligatory upon the fuller to restore what he handed over to someone else, if the fuller was trustworthy?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "He is liable for it unless he is trustworthy and reliable, if Allah wills."

key_terms.الْفَقِيهِ: the Imam addressed as the jurist
key_terms.الْقَصَّارِ: the fuller or launderer entrusted with the garment
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a garment given into another's care
key_terms.مَأْمُونًا: regarded as safe and dependable in entrusted matters

ai.seo_question: Is a worker liable if he gives entrusted property to another person and it is lost?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability when entrusted property is passed from one worker to another and then lost. The ruling states that the one who transferred the item is liable, except in the case where the other party is trustworthy and reliable. It reflects principles of trust, responsibility, and compensation in entrusted property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3933 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Ali bin Mahbub, who said:

A man wrote to the 'Jurist' (Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as)) asking about a case where a person gave a garment to a launderer to clean, and the launderer then handed it over to another launderer to clean, but the garment was lost. Should the first launderer be required to compensate for what he entrusted to another?
Imam (as) wrote in reply: "He is liable for it unless the second launderer is trustworthy and reliable, God willing."
